newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court rejects case against CVRD selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court rejects case against CVRD selloff.

text.p: A Justice at Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), Brazil's highest court, rejected a request from two private lawyers seeking an injunction to halt next week's privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
"The request was not given and the case has been filed," an STF spokesman said.

The two lawyers had alleged irregularities in the bid specifications for CVRD's privatization, which is due to begin on April 29 when the government will auction 40 to 45 percent of the company's voting stock.

The STF spokesman said the high court was still due to consider two cases lodged by opponents of the the CVRD selloff and which sought to stop the sale. No date had been set for those hearings, the spokesman said.
Resistance to the CVRD selloff has stiffened over the past few weeks as the company's auction date approached.
Lawyers, unions, landless peasants, government workers and even Catholic bishops have expressed their opposition to the privatization of CVRD and urged the government to reconsider the sale.
One of Brazil's largest and most profitable state companies, CVRD is considered a model of public sector management.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said his administration decided to sell the company after he became convinced that the public sector did not have the financial resources to invest in production.
